principle: Find the Art Circle already latent inside the subject. The subject itself should become the Art Circle. What would an Art Circle be in this subject’s world?
rules: Exactly one meaningful failure of closure. The gap is the conceptual event, never a decorative notch.
The subject, material, space, or event itself performs the attempted closure. Do not impose a symbol onto an unrelated subject.
A perfect circle exists only as an idea. Closure may be irregular, elongated, biomorphic, architectural, figurative, environmental, optical, sculptural, or implied.
Vary size, thickness, proportions, shape, crop, orientation, and placement aggressively. Avoid repetitive large centered C shapes.
Vary gap location and explain why this particular material or subject fails to close there.
Vary medium. Let material behavior determine the interruption.
Favor elegant conceptual transformation over decorative symbolism.
Allow negative space, environment, light, shadow, and reflection to function as the Art Circle.
No unnecessary text, signatures, captions, or artist clichés in the artwork.

Translate artists into descriptive vocabulary: materials, spatial logic, gesture, surface, scale, color relationships, and conceptual concerns. Do not quote famous works or request direct style imitation.
